name: MANTRA Chain
rootCause: An attacker drained 720M MANTRA, worth $3.6 million per Mantra’s postmortem, through a confirmed Cosmos EVM underflow bug. The halt came too late for 94.7% of it, which had already reached an exchange. Three more chains fell to the same flaw days later.

descriptions.text: An attacker drained 720M MANTRA, worth $3.6 million per Mantra’s postmortem, through a confirmed Cosmos EVM underflow bug. The halt came too late for 94.7% of it, which had already reached an exchange. Three more chains fell to the same flaw days later.

An attacker exploited an unsigned integer underflow vulnerability in the upstream Cosmos EVM module to unauthorizedly transfer approximately 720.9 million MANTRA from two MANTRA-managed addresses (the burn address and a dormant genesis-era multisig). The chain was halted to contain the threat and later resumed after a v8.4.0 patch. No validator keys, admin privileges, or user funds were compromised.

MANTRA Chain halted block production between Aug. 20 and Aug. 22, 2026 after attackers exploited a reported arithmetic flaw in the upstream Cosmos EVM dependency used by the network’s EVM module. Public postmortem reporting states that about 720.9 million MANTRA tokens were moved from a burn address and a legacy multisig wallet, with an estimated impact near $3.6 million and no reported user fund losses. MANTRA’s published postmortem summaries and subsequent reporting attribute the incident to an arithmetic flaw in the upstream cosmos/evm dependency.
